reason: The full correctness audit over 1dd01581..9177257 produced 23 raw and 16 deduplicated findings; all 16 passed adversarial source verification. Input retry state, shop transitions, and mutation-process ownership expand implementation scope, so repository policy requires completing them before a new readiness gate and full audit.

boundary.startingEvent: A parsed reqmenu move is retried after an admission boundary, a hero crosses a generated-shop boundary, a completed object-pile transaction exposes its named or priced row, or a mutation command owns active wrapper, scope, wave, helper, and reporting state.
boundary.endingEvent: The original command semantics and source-shaped shop transition reach the next prompt atomically, or the mutation command exits or is cancelled with every owned process collected and every timeout attributable; all confirmed tests and contracts distinguish the fixed behavior.
boundary.validInputs: Parsed reqmenu movement and retry; generated-shop strict-interior, edge, and debt-free exit transitions; supported billed-departure refusal; ordinary dropy; multibyte named pile rows; quantity stacks and quote partitions; mutation wrapper completion, signals, concurrent refusal, timeouts, and detached helpers.
boundary.observables: Pending command state, nopick/autopickup, hero and room state, achievement/billing/keeper state, messages, screens, cursors, PRNG log, floor ownership, exact byte rows and prices, quote extrema, process results/signals, cgroup ownership, descendant cleanup, timeout identities, and subsequent invocation availability.
boundary.exclusions: Unported shop billing/debit settlement remains fail-closed before movement; the full shop-edge blocking dialogue remains deferred behind an atomic admission stop; no sealed holdout evidence is used. Other prior generated-shop price exclusions remain unchanged.

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: Traced hack.c domove_core through pickup.c check_here and invent.c look_here's single-object and pile doname_with_price call sites, then objnam.c doname_base(DONAME_WITH_PRICE) and shk.c get_cost_of_shop_item, get_pricing_units, get_cost, getprice, oid_price_adjustment, and record_price_quote.
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: Cross-checked object classes and oc_cost data, generated SHTYPES rooms and keepers, quantity and Charisma partitions, quote sentinels, inventory currency wording, room-number buffers, and pile_limit's count-versus-menu split.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Followed get_obj_location, in_rooms, inside_shop, shop_keeper, inhishop, ordinary naming, price rounding, currency, and the object-chain loop. contained_cost and billing are excluded because valid objects are top-level non-containers.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: Inspected js/hack.js costly_spot refusal, js/invent.js look_here preflight and both naming sites, js/objnam.js preflight/discovery ownership, js/shk.js generated-shop queries and quote helpers, js/light.js object location, js/rooms.js current-shop state, and existing shop/object-pile tests and fresh runners.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: The fresh case validates a natural single generated-shop stock object because stock_room creates one object per square; a direct movement integration must separately prove the reviewed two-member menu and its atomic excluded-second-member refusal.

entries.reachability: The unmarked CLI has launched a long mutation run and receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, or a concurrent invocation is refused while another run owns the exclusivity lock.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs outer launcher and exclusivity owner
entries.effects: Forward cancellation only to the owned run, await cleanup, reproduce the caller-visible signal, and prevent a refused contender from stopping the owner.
entries.evidence: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs now acquires an owner-record lock, launches systemd-run asynchronously, forwards SIGINT and SIGTERM through its uniquely named aggregate slice, awaits cleanup, and re-raises the signal. The real-process regression refuses a contender while the owner remains live, cancels the owner with SIGTERM, confirms the slice is inactive, then proves the next invocation can acquire the lock. A stale-lock regression stops the dead owner's recorded slice before replacement.

entries.reachability: The outer mutator owns an active per-wave scope under memory/task limits and is cancelled or resource-limited.
entries.effects: Place outer and wave scopes beneath one uniquely owned aggregate slice so limits and cancellation contain the full process tree.
entries.evidence: Each invocation creates one underscore-named aggregate slice with the 2 GiB, zero-swap and 64-task limits. mutationCgroupArgs and testRunnerCommand place the outer scope and every production wave beneath it. The live outer regression reads both ControlGroup values and proves the scope is a descendant of the slice; command-shape tests pin the same ancestry for waves.

sourceReview: The full audit used correctness, readability, test-quality, variable-flow, and concurrency finders over 1dd01581..9177257. It produced 23 raw findings, deduplicated them to 16, and two independent adjudicators confirmed all 16 with no warning or unverified item. Exact-window mutation ran 204 sites, killed 194, left ten survivors, and timed out five; six shop survivors are proven equivalents, while the dropy survivor and remaining boundary survivors are assigned above. Because confirmed fixes change input retry, shop-transition, and process-lifecycle ownership, the pass returns to implementation and cannot close until a new readiness gate and full audit cover the expanded range.
